explain.title: Mean
explain.body: The mean, also known as the average, is the sum of all the values in a data set divided by the number of values. It represents the central value of a data set.

explain.title: Median
explain.body: The median is the middle value of a data set when the values are arranged in ascending or descending order. If the number of values is odd, the median is the middle value. If the number of values is even, the median is the average of the two middle values.

explain.title: Finding the median
explain.body: Arrange the data in ascending order first. For an odd number of values, use position (n + 1)/2. For an even number of values, average the values at positions n/2 and n/2 + 1.

explain.title: Mode
explain.body: The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set may have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode at all.

explain.title: Finding the mode
explain.body: Count the frequency of each value in the data set. The value with the highest frequency is the mode. If two or more values share the highest frequency, they are all modes; if every value occurs equally often, there is no mode.

mistakes: Finding the median before arranging the values in order.
Choosing just one of the two middle values when the number of values is even; take their average instead.
Dividing the sum by the wrong number of values when calculating the mean.
Assuming a data set always has a mode; it can have more than one mode or no mode.
Giving a mode without checking which value has the highest frequency.

explain.title: What a bar chart shows
explain.body: A bar chart is a graphical representation of data using bars of different heights or lengths. It is used to compare the quantities of different categories. Bar charts are effective for comparing different categories and visually representing the distribution of data.

explain.body: Label the x-axis with categories and the y-axis with values. Choose a scale that covers the data range and divide the axis into equal intervals.

explain.title: Drawing and labelling bars

explain.title: What biostatistics does
explain.body: Biostatistics applies statistical methods to biological sciences. It helps people use biological and health data to understand problems and make decisions.

explain.title: Mean: share the total equally
explain.body: To find the mean, add all the values and divide by the number of values. It is the arithmetic average.

explain.title: Median: find the middle
explain.body: Put the values in order. If there is an odd number of values, use the single middle value. If there is an even number, average the two middle values.

explain.title: Mode: find what occurs most
explain.body: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently. A data set may have more than one mode, or no mode if no value is repeated.

explain.title: Bar charts show category values
explain.body: A bar chart displays values for categories. Usually, categories go on the horizontal axis and values go on the vertical axis; each bar's height or length represents its category's value.

mistakes: Finding the median before ordering the values.

Dividing the sum by the wrong number of values when calculating the mean.
Calling the most frequent value the mean or median instead of the mode.
Forgetting that a data set can have two modes or no mode.
Leaving the axes or title unlabeled on a bar chart, or drawing bars that do not match the data values.

notes.title: Introduction to Biostatistics
notes.answer: Biostatistics applies statistical methods to biological sciences and helps people use biological and health data.
notes.explanation: Biostatistics uses statistical methods to help study biological and health-related questions. It helps researchers plan studies, analyse data, interpret results, predict outcomes, and support public health decisions.
notes.simple: Biostatistics is statistics used in biology and health.
examples: Analysing COVID-19 rates can help guide vaccination campaigns.
Comparing wheat yields can help researchers assess different varieties and farming practices.
steps: Plan a study so that it collects relevant and sufficient data.
Analyse the data to find trends, correlations, and patterns.
Interpret the results so they can guide decisions.
Use current data to predict outcomes and plan actions.
notes.checkQuestion: What can biostatistics help public health officials do with data about disease rates?
notes.checkAnswer: Biostatistics is a branch of statistics that applies statistical methods to biological sciences.

notes.title: Mean, Median, and Mode
notes.answer: Mean = sum of all data points divided by number of data points; median = the middle value after ordering; mode = the most frequent value.
notes.explanation: Mean, median, and mode describe the centre or most common value in a data set. Find the mean by adding all the values and dividing by how many there are. Find the median after arranging the values in order. Find the mode by checking which value occurs most often.
notes.simple: Mean is the sharing-out average, median is the middle after sorting, and mode is the value that occurs most often.
examples: For 2, 4, 6, the median is 4, and there is no mode because no value repeats.
steps: For the mean, add all the data values and divide by the number of values.
For the median, arrange the values in ascending order.
If there are an odd number of values, take the middle value; if there are an even number, average the two middle values.
For the mode, count how often each value appears and choose the value or values with the highest frequency.
notes.checkAnswer: The values in order are 2, 4, 8, 10. The two middle values are 4 and 8, so the median is (4 + 8)/2 = 6.

notes.title: Reading and making a bar chart
notes.answer: A bar chart represents data using bars of different heights or lengths to compare categories.
notes.explanation: A bar chart uses bars to show the values of different categories, so you can compare them quickly.
notes.simple: Each category gets a bar. The bar’s height shows that category’s value.
examples: If Species A has 15 plants, its bar reaches 15 on the value axis.
If Species D has 25 plants, its bar is taller than the bar for Species A.
steps: Arrange the categories and their values.
Draw and label the x-axis and y-axis.
Choose a suitable scale with equal intervals.
Draw equal-width bars, spaced evenly, to the correct values.
Label each bar with its category and value.
notes.checkQuestion: What does the height of a bar show?
notes.checkAnswer: The value of the corresponding category.

notes.title: Biostatistics and ways to summarise data
notes.answer: Biostatistics applies statistical methods to biological sciences. Mean, median, mode, and bar charts help describe and interpret data.
notes.explanation: Biostatistics applies statistical methods to biological sciences. It helps organise and understand data so people can make informed decisions, for example in public health. The mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values; the median is the middle value when the data is ordered; and the mode is the most frequently occurring value. A bar chart uses bars to show the values of different categories.
notes.simple: Biostatistics helps us use data about living things and health. Mean is the average, median is the middle, and mode is the most common value.
examples: For 3, 5, 5, 8, the median is (5 + 5) ÷ 2 = 5 and the mode is 5.
steps: Order the values from smallest to largest when finding the median.
For an odd number of values, select the single middle value; for an even number, average the two middle values.
To find the mean, add all values and divide by the number of values.
To find the mode, identify the value or values occurring most frequently.
For a bar chart, place categories on the horizontal axis and show each category's value with a bar.

quiz.stem: A researcher uses statistical methods to study data about living organisms. Which field is the researcher using?
options: It applies statistical methods to biological sciences.
It replaces experiments with opinions.
It studies only the structure of cells.
It records financial transactions.
rationales: Correct: applying statistical methods to biological sciences is biostatistics.
Incorrect: biostatistics supports the analysis of evidence; it does not replace experiments with opinions.
Incorrect: biostatistics is not limited to studying cell structure.
Incorrect: financial transactions are not the focus of biostatistics.

quiz.stem: How does biostatistics help when a biological experiment is being planned?
options: To make sure collected data are relevant and sufficient for the research question.
To guarantee that every study gives the expected result.
To avoid collecting any data.
To choose the final policy before studying the evidence.
rationales: Correct: it helps structure a study so its data can answer the research question.
Incorrect: careful planning cannot guarantee a particular result.
Incorrect: studies need data to answer research questions.
Incorrect: decisions should be informed by evidence, not chosen before the evidence is studied.

quiz.stem: What may analysing biological data help researchers discover?
options: It can reveal trends, correlations, and patterns in the data.
It changes the data so that the results look stronger.
It proves that every observed relationship is causal.
It removes the need to interpret results.
rationales: Correct: analysis can uncover trends, correlations, and patterns.
Incorrect: analysis should examine data, not alter it to strengthen a result.
Incorrect: a correlation alone does not prove that one factor caused another.
Incorrect: results still need to be interpreted meaningfully.

quiz.stem: Which is an example of biostatistics helping to interpret results?
options: Interpreting disease survey results to guide public health interventions.
Choosing a treatment without examining any evidence.
Predicting weather from plant names alone.
Counting laboratory equipment for an inventory.
rationales: Correct: interpreting disease prevalence results can guide public health interventions.
Incorrect: biostatistics uses evidence to inform decisions rather than ignore it.
Incorrect: the example does not use biological data to predict an outcome.
Incorrect: an equipment inventory is not an example of interpreting biological results.

quiz.stem: Which task is an example of predicting outcomes with biostatistics?
options: Using current data to model the likely spread of an infectious disease.
Changing the results of a completed study.
Listing the names of diseases alphabetically.
Selecting a vaccine without considering disease data.
rationales: Correct: models can use current data to predict how an infectious disease may spread.
Incorrect: results should not be changed to fit an expectation.
Incorrect: alphabetical listing is not prediction from data.
Incorrect: vaccine planning should use evidence about disease and health outcomes.

quiz.stem: Why is biostatistics useful in public health and policy making?
options: It provides evidence-based insights for health policies and guidelines.
It ensures that public health decisions need no evidence.
It is used only after a disease has disappeared.
It prevents researchers from comparing treatments.
rationales: Correct: evidence from statistical analysis can guide policies and health guidelines.
Incorrect: biostatistics helps decisions rely on evidence.
Incorrect: it can be used to study current health problems and plan responses.
Incorrect: biostatistics can support comparisons, including in clinical trials.

quiz.stem: Find the mean of 8, 10, 14, and 16.
rationales: Incorrect: the sum is 48, and 48 divided by 4 is not 10.
Incorrect: 14 is one of the data values, but it is not their mean.
Incorrect: 16 is the greatest value, not the mean.

quiz.stem: What is the median of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11?
rationales: Incorrect: 5 is the second value, not the middle value.
Correct: the ordered set has five values, so its third value, 7, is the median.
Incorrect: 9 is the fourth value, not the middle value.
Incorrect: 11 is the greatest value, not the middle value.

quiz.stem: Find the median of 4, 8, 6, 10.
rationales: Incorrect: after ordering, 4 is the first value.
Incorrect: 6 is one of the middle values, but the median is their average.
Correct: the ordered values are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the median is (6 + 8)/2 = 7.
Incorrect: 8 is one of the middle values, but the median is their average.

quiz.stem: What is the mode of 2, 3, 3, 4, 5?
rationales: Incorrect: 2 appears only once.
Correct: 3 appears twice, more often than any other value.
Incorrect: 4 appears only once.
Incorrect: 5 appears only once.

quiz.stem: Identify the mode or modes of 2, 2, 4, 4, 7.
options: There is no mode
2 and 4
2 only
4 only
rationales: Incorrect: 2 and 4 both occur more often than 7.
Correct: 2 and 4 each occur twice, the highest frequency, so both are modes.
Incorrect: 2 is a mode, but 4 also occurs twice.
Incorrect: 4 is a mode, but 2 also occurs twice.

quiz.stem: Which description gives the mode of a data set?
options: The smallest value
The largest value
The middle value after arranging the data
The value that occurs most often
rationales: Incorrect: the smallest value is not necessarily the most frequent.
Incorrect: the largest value is not necessarily the most frequent.
Incorrect: this describes the median, not the mode.
Correct: the mode is the value that appears most frequently.

The number of bars shows how many categories there are, not a single bar’s height.

options: The horizontal x-axis

quiz.stem: Q11.5. What is the mean of the data set: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11?
rationales: This is incorrect because 7 is not the sum divided by the number of values.

quiz.stem: Q11.8. If a data set has no repeated values, what is the mode?

quiz.stem: Q11.9. In a bar chart, what does the height or length of each bar represent?
